source.title: Measuring the Depth of LLM Unlearning via Activation Patching
source.authors: Jaeung Lee; Dohyun Kim; Jaemin Jo

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure text is garbled and some table layout is flattened, but the relevant results are described in the main text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses causal activation patching to test whether knowledge remains recoverable after unlearning, and measures recovery after fine-tuning. It uses different procedures and measures from the claim's cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports 4-bit quantization results for the stability of evaluation metrics, not direct targeted-knowledge recovery after quantization; those are not recorded as D rows. It does not test activation-direction ablation or prompt-only attacks. Quantization and relearning values in Table 3 are aggregate metric-robustness scores, not raw task accuracy.
record.test_reason: The study applies cross-model activation patching (UDS) to 150 TOFU-unlearned Llama-3.2-1B models from 8 methods. UDS measures how much forget-set knowledge stays causally recoverable inside models that output-level metrics count as unlearned, which bears directly on version C (access blocked rather than knowledge deleted). Its one-epoch relearning on Df gives indirect, text-stated evidence on B: the authors say residual knowledge lets generation recover faster than the retain model learns the facts. It is a metric paper, but its case studies and Table 6 report internal residual knowledge per method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors propose UDS, a two-stage activation-patching metric, and find it the most faithful and robust of 20 metrics. Case studies show residual knowledge that output-level and observational metrics miss, with erasure depth varying across prompt types. They say one epoch of relearning rapidly restores generation by realigning the output space without substantially altering deeply encoded knowledge, so UDS stays stable. On that basis they recommend UDS as a substitute for post-perturbation evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and evaluates UDS, a two-stage activation-patching metric, rather than a new unlearning recipe. Its relearning test fine-tunes on Df for one epoch.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported erasure depth varies by prompt type and unlearning method; the authors also report that UDS scores vary across examples.
record.problems: The evaluation focuses on TOFU; the reported fine-tuning attack uses Df rather than unrelated, loosely related, or subset relearning data. Activation patching is an indirect measure of recoverability, and the paper notes limitations to localized entity spans and the need for a retain model for calibrated UDS.
record.rows_left_out: No direct targeted-knowledge results after quantization were reported; the quantization plots and Table 3 values assess metric stability. No raw per-model relearning scores were extracted beyond the aggregate results described in Table 3 and §4.2.

untested.parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance is reported together with utility and attack results. Only filtering at ≥80% utility is reported.
No small, unrelated, loosely related or subset relearning sets; relearning is one epoch on the full Df. No raw recovered accuracy is reported, only R stability scores.
No single activation-direction ablation. Residual knowledge is shown by cross-model patching into Mfull, not by extracting the answer from the unlearned model itself.
4-bit NF4 quantization is applied only to assess metric stability. No targeted-knowledge restoration rate is reported in readable form.
No rephrasing, jailbreak or in-context attack is reported as a recovery result. Jailbreak-ROUGE appears only as a metric scored for stability.
No new unlearning method is proposed. UDS is an evaluation metric.

missing.what: Across all IdkNLL configurations, every normalized MIA score is ≈0.0 (read as erased), yet UDS ranges only 0.039–0.253, indicating residual internal knowledge.

Per-metric counts of models showing recovery ('rec') vs destruction after 4-bit quantization and after relearning. The figure text is garbled and the counts are unreadable, but they bear on quantization-based and relearning recovery.

Layer-wise LER for the IdkDPO example: Logit Lens gives LER=1.000 at layers 7–13 while UDS gives LER ≤0.230, with the two converging at 0.254 at the final layer. This shows internal knowledge persisting behind an apparent erasure.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Single architecture (Llama-3.2-1B) and TOFU only, although Table 2 validates UDS across 1B/3B/8B on retain splits, not on unlearned models. The Table 6 rows are best configurations chosen by a selection formula, so they are not representative of each method. UDS caps at 1, so over-unlearning is indistinguishable from perfect erasure. Residual knowledge is shown by patching the unlearned model's states into Mfull; this demonstrates latent information, not an attack on the deployed model.

versions.untested_parts: It filters for models preserving at least 80% utility and classified as unlearned, but does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance alongside those utility results and attack outcomes as this version requires.
Tests one epoch of fine-tuning on the forget set Df, not unrelated or loosely related examples, a few examples, or a subset of forgotten facts.
Tests recoverability through activation patching and discusses access-blocking versus erasure; it does not ablate a single activation direction.
Quantization is applied in the metric-robustness evaluation, but the reported results concern metric stability rather than whether targeted knowledge is restored.
No prompt-only recovery attack using rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information is tested.
UDS is an evaluation metric, not a counter-unlearning method tested for resisting the listed attacks.

relation.reason: Its UDS results bear on version C. For B it gives only metric-stability scores.

tranche.reason: It is a new activation-patching metric aimed at the depth-of-erasure (block vs delete) question, with no new unlearning recipe.

source_check.notes: All unlearning results use one TOFU-finetuned Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct setup (1B/3B/8B appear only for the retain-split check). Table 5 is one IdkNLL model, Table 4 is one IdkDPO example, and Table 6 gives one best configuration per method, picked by an output-level formula. Normalized MIA: higher means erased, so IdkNLL's about 0.0 means MIA still detects the forget set. UDS is clipped at 1, so over-unlearning cannot be told apart from erasure.

statements.correction: 2605.24614 (Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, TOFU forget10, 1 epoch on full Df): ROUGE-variant relearning stability R 0.064-0.203. The text says generation recovery far exceeds what the retain model learns in one epoch. It gives no recovery magnitudes.
statements.problem: Cites this study (r1) as evidence that unlearned models relearn faster than a control but describes no finding for it. r1 is a symmetric ROUGE stability score R and cannot show recovery. The direction is only in the authors' words, and relearning uses the whole Df, not a small or partial set.

States nothing explicit about this study, and its numbers belong to other studies. The citation fits: under the same 1-epoch relearn, ROUGE R is 0.203 while UDS R is 0.900, and the authors say generation recovers while UDS-measured knowledge barely changes.

statements.correction: IdkNLL UDS (one model): person name 0.025, book/title 0.038, biographical 0.049, Yes/No 0.624. IdkNLL best configuration 0.251 with MIAagg 0.000 (all IdkNLL configurations about 0.0 on normalized MIA, UDS 0.039-0.253). IdkDPO: one example UDS 0.209 vs Logit Lens 0.801 (Table 4); best configuration UDS 0.686, MIAagg 0.757. Higher normalized MIA means erasure.
statements.problem: Applies the 0.025-0.251 range to IdkNLL/IdkDPO, but IdkDPO's 0.209 is one example and its best configuration is 0.686. IdkNLL Yes/No is 0.624. 'Output/MIA metrics indicate erasure' is wrong for IdkNLL, whose normalized MIA is about 0.0 (MIAagg 0.000), meaning no erasure by MIA. In the IdkDPO example, the reading of erasure comes from Logit Lens. UDS patches unlearned states into Mfull, not original components into the unlearned model.
None. The values come from one IdkNLL model (Table 5).
Makes no claim about this study, so there is nothing to be wrong. Optionally, its causal UDS patching (which needs Mfull) could be listed with the causal part of the blocking clause.
